History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
31-year-old postpartum female with sudden-onset shortness of breath one hour ago; concern for pulmonary embolism, advised immediate hospital evaluation.

History:
• Chief complaint: Acute shortness of breath that began suddenly ~1 hour ago while sitting and watching TV.  
• Course: No prior similar episodes. Symptoms have remained present but not clearly progressive during the call.  
• Associated symptoms:
  – Non-productive cough started yesterday.  
  – Palpitations (“my heart, it’s really going”).  
  – Chest soreness on deep inspiration, but no constant chest pain.  
  – No hemoptysis mentioned.  
• Exacerbating / relieving factors: None identified.  
• Pertinent ROS negatives (stated or implied): No mention of fever, leg swelling, calf pain, syncope.  
• Notable background: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago; incision still tender. No other chronic illnesses reported.

Past Medical History:
• Cesarean section 4 weeks prior (post-operative course: taking codeine for pain; stopped ~1 week ago).  
• No other chronic medical conditions reported.  
• Allergies: Ibuprofen – reaction unspecified (“allergic to Ibuprofen”; patient unsure of reaction details).  
• Medications: Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented); not taken for the last week.

Social History:
• Lives at home with newborn; partner at work during consult.  
• No data provided regarding smoking, alcohol, or recreational drug use.

Family History:
• Mother has history of leg clots (probable DVT).

Physical Examination:
(Conducted via telehealth)
• Pulse: Patient counted 30 beats during provider-timed count (duration not documented); clinician interpreted as “slightly fast.”  
• No additional vitals or physical findings documented.

Investigations:
• None performed during call.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute shortness of breath in postpartum period – possible pulmonary embolism
  • Assessment: Sudden SOB, mild tachycardia, postpartum status (4 weeks post-C-section) → high index of suspicion for venous thromboembolism (PE).  
  • Plan:
    – Advise immediate hospital evaluation for further work-up (ECG, D-dimer, CT pulmonary angiography, blood gases as per ED protocol).  
    – Discussed transport options: ambulance vs. self-transport; patient elected self-transport with newborn and essentials.  
    – Instructed to go “fairly quickly.”  
    – Advised to withhold Codeine until evaluated.  
    – Explained possibility of anticoagulation therapy if clot confirmed.  
    – Provided reassurance and opportunity for questions; patient declined further questions.

General plan items:
• Advise patient to seek emergency services if symptoms worsen en route.  
• Document allergy to Ibuprofen in hospital records.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: Comprehensive vitals (BP, RR, SpO₂, temperature); full medication list; detailed allergy reaction; surgical discharge summary; smoking/alcohol history.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational filler words; no major inaudible sections.
